text.p: Indonesia's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur said its shareholders approved on Thursday the firm's proposed 1.55 trillion rupiah acquisition of six sister companies in the Salim Group.

"Indofood expects its 1997 net profit to grow by more than 45 percent and earnings per share by more than 20 percent after the acquisitions," chief executive officer Eva Riyanti Hutapea told reporters after a shareholders' meeting.
Eva also said shareholders had approved the firm's proposed 5:1 rights issue to partly finance the acquisitions.
Indofood posted a net profit of 351.3 billion rupiah in 1996, while earnings per share was 230 rupiah.
Indofood expected to raise 1.007 trillion rupiah from the rights issue.
The remaining 543 billion rupiah for the acquisitions was expected to come from bank loans.
Indofood plans to acquire firms in the oil palm plantations business, a cooking oil producer, a palm oil trader and a distribution firm.
Eva said the aquisitions were expected to boost the firm's distribution capabilities and expand its product ranges.
"The acquisitions would boost the firm's performance which will automatically increase the earnings per share growth even on a fully diluted basis," Eva said.
"Without the acquisitions, Indofood's EPS growth this year would be around 15 percent, but with the acquisitions the growth would be more than 20 percent," he said.

Indofood director Angel Umali said the firms to be acquired were expected to account for 36 percent of expected total Indofood net sales in 1997 and 31 percent of the firm's operating profit during the period.
